The Paradox of Exchange
ACTIVATION:
REALIZED USE-VALU
The Contradiction
• For the Owner: The commodity is a non-use-value (merely a
physical depository of exchange-value).
• For the Non-Owner: The commodity must be a use-value
(satisfying a specific need).
EXCHANGE-VALUE
REALIZATION
The Resolution: Mutual Alienation
Commodities must be entirely alienated; they must enter into the
exchange process... only by being realized as exchange-values can
they be realized as use-values. Social labor only proves itself as
universal labor after this process supersedes its original character.

The Transformation:

The Shift
Because all commodities measure their exchange-value
against one specific commodity, that excluded commodity
(the linen) becomes the adequate representation of
exchange-value.
The Result
The infinite equations collapse into a single two-term
equation. The labor-time in the linen becomes the direct,
visible embodiment of universal social labor.

The Material Veil
The Mystification
Only the conventions of everyday life make it appear
ordinary that social relations of production assume
the shape of physical things.
The Core Truth
Although it is thus correct to say that exchange-value

Social Relations
The Error of Economists
The illusions of the Monetary System arise from
viewing money purely as a physical object, failing to
perceive it as a materialized social relation of production.

From Barter to Circulation
Phase 1: The Border
Exchange happens not
within communities, but
on their margins where
different tribes meet.
Phase 2: The Disintegration
Barter moves into the interior,
exerting a disintegrating influence
on the communal system.
The Evolution
Direct barter is the beginning of the
transformation. Use-values become
commodities only when a larger amount is
produced than is required for survival.
The Catalyst
The gradual extension of barter and
variety of goods traded stimulates
the formation of money.
The Fallacy

technical device" cleverlv invented to solve
inconveniences.
Marx counters: Money evolved necessarily
